required.rationale: Stage 1 of HF-DB-006-SOCIAL-007. Replaces the USING (true) SELECT policy on public.post_likes (20240430000000_create_posts.sql:47-49), public.post_comments (20241220000010_enhance_feed_system.sql:131-134) and public.comment_likes (:152-155) with policies scoped TO authenticated and predicated on the parent row being readable. Measured on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster: before the migration an unauthenticated caller reads 2 of 2 post_likes rows, 1 of 1 comment_likes rows and 2 of 2 post_comments rows; after it reads 0 of each. That is a platform-wide identity and engagement graph exposed to the internet, and it is a security defect, not a type error. No committed product surface changes behaviour, so this is not blocked on a consumer change; stage 2 (own-rows plus entitled engagement readers) is a separate, smaller follow-up that IS blocked on the social and admin lanes.

required.rationale: The two MONEY-PATH items of HF-DB-011-MARKETPLACE-CHAIN-SURFACE-AUTHORED, selected from the 46 blocking items the disposition instrument classifies out of 66 archived marketplace surface items. public.marketplace_payment_events (archive 20260728000011:45-79) is the Stripe webhook idempotency claim: without its unique constraint on provider_event_id, a retried checkout.session.completed fulfils an order twice. Its RLS design is enabled-with-no-policy so only a role that bypasses RLS can reach it, reproduced verbatim. public.marketplace_fee_rules (archive 20260728000010) is the versioned platform fee schedule, admin-write-only behind public.profiles.role = 'admin' with no public read; its two real readers, lib/marketplace/fee-calculator.ts:51-57 via app/api/marketplace/checkout/route.ts:352 and app/api/marketplace/admin/fee-rules/route.ts, both use createServiceRoleClient(), which is why the archive's no-public-read design is correct rather than a bug. The default rule is seeded INACTIVE so applying the migration cannot start charging a fee. The remaining 36 blocking items are the external-fulfilment surface from archive 20260704224927 and are one product decision the marketplace lane owns, not 36 independent column contracts.

required.rationale: HF-DB-011-SCHEDULED-POSTS-FRESH-CHAIN-DIVERGENCE, an ordering defect reproduced from the repository's own files rather than asserted. 20250904110000 adds scheduled_posts.platform_status and .platform_errors behind `alter table if exists`; the table is created later by 20260413200000 because '2026-04-13' sorts after '2025-09-04'. A fresh replay therefore creates the table and never the two columns, while app/api/artist/content/overview/route.ts:137 selects them and lib/services/cross-platform-posting.service.ts:195 writes one. The chain and the committed contract happen to agree (the contract does not declare them either), which is why regeneration loses nothing - but the live route breaks at PostgREST on a chain-built target. This migration repairs it forward. The earlier migration cannot be edited and renumbering would not move it after 20260413200000.
